intro:
A limit asks one question: as $x$ gets close to $a$, what number does $f(x)$ get close to? Here the curve is a road. In the Close in on a point tab you drive two cars toward $x = a$, one from each side; each car's tag reads $f(x)$ where its nose is, and a magnifier follows them in. In the Out to infinity tab the cars drive far out, and the height levels off.

The curves cover every way a limit can behave: a hole, a point out of place that you can move back, a jump, a vertical asymptote, an oscillation that never settles, the squeeze theorem and limits at infinity. The “?” button holds the table of values, the limits and the continuity check.
howItWorks:
Each car's nose is the point $(x, f(x))$ on the road, whose center line is exactly $y = f(x)$. Close in drives both cars to $x = a - 0.001$ and $x = a + 0.001$; the table behind “?” shows $h = 1, 0.1, 0.01, \ldots$ from each side.

  • Limit from the left $\lim_{x \to a^-} f(x)$: where $f(x)$ heads as $x$ comes up to $a$ from below (the purple car).
  • Limit from the right $\lim_{x \to a^+} f(x)$: from above (the orange car).
  • The limit $\lim_{x \to a} f(x)$ exists only when both one-sided limits exist and are equal. It never depends on $f(a)$.
  • Continuous at $a$: $f(a)$ is defined, the limit exists, and they are equal.

Test yourself has twelve kinds of problem; each unlocks with the lesson that teaches it. A first try counts toward your progress, and a miss goes to your review queue.
